easy: A person who loves doing exciting and risky things.

ex.en: The adventurer climbed the tallest mountain in the world.
ex.ko: 그 모험가는 세계에서 가장 높은 산에 올랐다.

easy: A round, chewy bread with a hole in the middle.

ex.en: I had a toasted bagel with cream cheese for breakfast.
ex.ko: 나는 아침으로 크림치즈를 바른 구운 베이글을 먹었다.

easy: A person from a group of people who live in the mountains between Spain and France.

ex.en: The Basque shepherd led his sheep up the green hills.
ex.ko: 바스크인 목동이 양 떼를 몰고 푸른 언덕을 올라갔다.

easy: A person who unfairly dislikes people who are different and won't listen to other ideas.

ex.en: Only a bigot would say that girls can't play soccer.
ex.ko: 편견이 심한 사람이나 여자아이는 축구를 못 한다고 말할 것이다.

easy: A long, fluffy scarf made of feathers.

ex.en: She wore a pink feather boa in the dress-up game.
ex.ko: 그녀는 옷 입기 놀이에서 분홍색 깃털 목도리를 둘렀다.

easy: Bars or lumps of gold or silver.

ex.en: The bank vault was full of shiny gold bullion.
ex.ko: 은행 금고는 반짝이는 금괴로 가득했다.

easy: A person who works in a government office and follows lots of rules.

ex.en: The bureaucrat said we had to fill out three more forms.
ex.ko: 그 관료는 우리가 서류를 세 장 더 작성해야 한다고 말했다.

easy: The meat of a carp, a big freshwater fish, eaten as food.

ex.en: Grandma baked carp with lemon and herbs.
ex.ko: 할머니는 잉어를 레몬과 허브를 넣어 구우셨다.

easy: To complain about small, unimportant things.

ex.en: He carped about the color of the plates at dinner.
ex.ko: 그는 저녁 식사 때 접시 색깔을 두고 트집을 잡았다.

easy: The distance all the way around a circle or round object.

ex.en: We measured the circumference of the tree trunk with a string.
ex.ko: 우리는 끈으로 나무 줄기의 둘레를 쟀다.

easy: In a smart and clever way.

ex.en: The fox cleverly hid its tracks in the snow.
ex.ko: 여우는 눈 위의 발자국을 교묘하게 감췄다.

easy: To give a place computers or put information onto computers.

ex.en: The library computerized its book list so you can search it online.
ex.ko: 도서관은 책 목록을 전산화해서 온라인으로 검색할 수 있게 했다.

easy: Sad and let down after finding out that something is not as good as you believed.

ex.en: He felt disillusioned when he learned the magic show was all tricks.
ex.ko: 그는 마술 쇼가 모두 속임수라는 것을 알고 실망했다.

easy: In the Bible, the last day of the world, when God judges everyone.

ex.en: The old painting showed angels blowing trumpets on Doomsday.
ex.ko: 그 오래된 그림에는 최후의 심판일에 나팔을 부는 천사들이 그려져 있었다.

easy: A person who drinks something.

ex.en: My little brother is a big milk drinker.
ex.ko: 내 남동생은 우유를 엄청 많이 마신다.

easy: Stuck deep in something messy or complicated.

ex.en: She got entangled in an argument between her two friends.
ex.ko: 그녀는 두 친구 사이의 말다툼에 휘말렸다.

easy: Done to explore or find out more about something.

ex.en: The robot made an exploratory trip into the dark cave.
ex.ko: 로봇이 어두운 동굴로 탐사를 떠났다.

easy: Skill in handling a tricky situation gently and cleverly.

ex.en: Our teacher used finesse to stop the fight without anyone getting upset.
ex.ko: 선생님은 아무도 기분 상하지 않게 솜씨 좋게 싸움을 말리셨다.

easy: A very bright meteor that streaks across the sky, sometimes exploding.

ex.en: We saw a fireball light up the night sky over the lake.
ex.ko: 우리는 호수 위 밤하늘을 환하게 밝히는 큰 별똥별을 보았다.

easy: A soft, warm cloth used to make shirts and pajamas.

ex.en: I wear flannel pajamas on cold winter nights.
ex.ko: 나는 추운 겨울밤에 플란넬 잠옷을 입는다.

easy: Soft colored thread used for sewing pictures on cloth.

ex.en: She used red floss to stitch a heart on her pillow.
ex.ko: 그녀는 빨간 자수실로 베개에 하트를 수놓았다.

easy: To clean between your teeth with a thin string.

ex.en: The dentist told me to floss every night.
ex.ko: 치과 의사 선생님이 매일 밤 치실질을 하라고 하셨다.

easy: About the heat deep inside the earth.

ex.en: Iceland uses geothermal heat to warm its houses.
ex.ko: 아이슬란드는 지열로 집을 데운다.

easy: The main idea of what someone said or wrote.

ex.en: I didn't hear every word, but I got the gist of the story.
ex.ko: 모든 말을 다 듣진 못했지만 이야기의 요점은 알았다.

easy: A small square of cloth for wiping your nose or eyes.

ex.en: Grandpa gave me his handkerchief when I started to cry.
ex.ko: 내가 울기 시작하자 할아버지가 손수건을 건네주셨다.

easy: A place where you can plug into electricity, water, or other services.

ex.en: Our campsite had an electric hookup for the camper.
ex.ko: 우리 캠핑장에는 캠핑카용 전기 연결 장치가 있었다.

easy: In a way that seems impossible to fix.

ex.en: My headphone cords were hopelessly tangled.
ex.ko: 내 헤드폰 줄이 어찌할 수 없을 만큼 엉켜 있었다.

easy: Freedom from being punished.

ex.en: The cat stole fish from the table with impunity, since no one saw.
ex.ko: 아무도 보지 못해서 고양이는 식탁의 생선을 훔치고도 혼나지 않았다.

easy: Giving facts and information.

ex.en: The museum had an informational video about volcanoes.
ex.ko: 박물관에는 화산에 관한 정보 영상이 있었다.

easy: Not having enough money to pay what you owe.

ex.en: The store closed because of insolvency.
ex.ko: 그 가게는 빚을 갚을 수 없어 문을 닫았다.

easy: As a joke, not seriously.

ex.en: Dad jokingly said he would eat all the birthday cake himself.
ex.ko: 아빠는 생일 케이크를 혼자 다 먹겠다고 농담으로 말씀하셨다.

easy: In terms of math.

ex.en: It is mathematically impossible to split 3 cookies equally between 2 people without breaking one.
ex.ko: 쿠키 3개를 하나도 쪼개지 않고 2명이 똑같이 나누는 것은 수학적으로 불가능하다.

easy: A tiny living thing, too small to see, especially one that can make you sick.

ex.en: Wash your hands to get rid of microbes.
ex.ko: 손을 씻어서 세균을 없애라.

easy: To get people or things ready to act.

ex.en: The town mobilized volunteers to fill sandbags before the flood.
ex.ko: 마을은 홍수가 오기 전에 모래주머니를 채울 자원봉사자를 동원했다.

easy: A state of working extra hard and fast.

ex.en: Before the holidays, the bakery goes into overdrive.
ex.ko: 명절 전이면 빵집은 정신없이 바빠진다.

easy: To make someone work too hard.

ex.en: The coach overdrove the team, and everyone was exhausted.
ex.ko: 코치가 팀을 혹사해서 모두 녹초가 되었다.

easy: A Jewish holiday in spring that remembers how the Israelites escaped from Egypt.

ex.en: My friend's family eats flat bread called matzah at Passover.
ex.ko: 내 친구네 가족은 유월절에 마차라는 납작한 빵을 먹는다.

easy: A small dog from China with short legs, long silky hair, and a flat face.

ex.en: The fluffy Peke snored on the couch.
ex.ko: 털이 복슬복슬한 페키니즈가 소파에서 코를 골았다.

easy: A big prison for people who did serious crimes.

ex.en: The bank robber was sent to the penitentiary for ten years.
ex.ko: 은행 강도는 10년 동안 교도소에 보내졌다.

easy: A college that teaches science, engineering, and practical skills.

ex.en: My uncle studied engineering at a polytechnic.
ex.ko: 삼촌은 공업 대학에서 공학을 공부했다.

easy: By many ordinary people.

ex.en: The tomato is popularly called a vegetable, but it is really a fruit.
ex.ko: 토마토는 흔히 채소라고 불리지만 사실은 과일이다.

easy: A group of people called together by a sheriff to help catch someone.

ex.en: In the western movie, the sheriff gathered a posse to chase the outlaws.
ex.ko: 서부 영화에서 보안관은 무법자들을 쫓으려고 추격대를 모았다.

easy: Keeping food cold or frozen so it stays fresh.

ex.en: Without refrigeration, milk goes bad quickly.
ex.ko: 냉장하지 않으면 우유는 금방 상한다.

easy: So bad that it makes you feel disgusted.

ex.en: Cheating to win was a repulsive thing to do.
ex.ko: 이기려고 속임수를 쓰는 것은 역겨운 짓이었다.

easy: A light sword with a curved handle used in fencing.

ex.en: She won the fencing match with her saber.
ex.ko: 그녀는 사브르로 펜싱 경기에서 이겼다.

easy: To do the samba, a lively dance from Brazil.

ex.en: Everyone sambaed in the street during the carnival.
ex.ko: 카니발 동안 모두가 거리에서 삼바를 추었다.

easy: Long, thick, and messy (about hair or fur).

ex.en: The shaggy dog needed a haircut.
ex.ko: 털이 덥수룩한 개는 털을 깎아야 했다.

easy: Not able to sleep.

ex.en: I spent a sleepless night before the big test.
ex.ko: 나는 큰 시험 전날 밤 한숨도 못 잤다.

easy: In music, a curved line over notes that means play them smoothly together.

ex.en: The slur over the notes told me to play them smoothly.
ex.ko: 음표 위의 이음줄을 보고 나는 부드럽게 이어서 연주했다.

easy: To grow bigger and bigger very fast, like a snowball rolling downhill.

ex.en: Our small bake sale snowballed into a huge town fair.
ex.ko: 우리의 작은 빵 바자회가 눈덩이처럼 커져 마을 축제가 되었다.

easy: To make something simpler and faster by removing extra steps or parts.

ex.en: We streamlined our morning routine so we don't miss the bus.
ex.ko: 우리는 버스를 놓치지 않으려고 아침 일과를 간소화했다.

easy: The amount a big spoon holds, used in cooking.

ex.en: Add one tablespoon of sugar to the batter.
ex.ko: 반죽에 설탕 한 큰술을 넣어라.

easy: Still a little sticky because it is not completely dry.

ex.en: Don't touch the bench; the paint is still tacky.
ex.ko: 벤치 만지지 마. 페인트가 아직 끈적거려.

easy: How much work or material goes through a system in a certain time.

ex.en: The new machine doubled the factory's throughput of toy cars.
ex.ko: 새 기계 덕분에 공장의 장난감 자동차 처리량이 두 배가 되었다.

easy: A stand with three legs that holds a camera or telescope steady.

ex.en: Dad put the camera on a tripod to take a family photo.
ex.ko: 아빠가 가족사진을 찍으려고 카메라를 삼각대에 올렸다.

easy: A spring flower shaped like a cup that grows from a bulb.

ex.en: Red and yellow tulips bloomed in our front yard.
ex.ko: 앞마당에 빨갛고 노란 튤립이 피었다.

easy: Long ago, a gate across a road that opened only after you paid money.

ex.en: The traveler paid a penny to pass the turnpike.
ex.ko: 여행자는 1페니를 내고 요금 징수 문을 지나갔다.

easy: A person whose job is to plan funerals and take care of dead bodies.

ex.en: The undertaker helped the family plan Grandpa's funeral.
ex.ko: 장의사가 가족이 할아버지 장례식을 준비하는 것을 도왔다.

easy: The US government service that delivers letters and packages.

ex.en: The USPS truck brings our mail every afternoon.
ex.ko: 미국 우체국 트럭이 매일 오후에 우리 우편물을 가져다준다.

easy: A person who tells others about something wrong happening where they work so it can be stopped.

ex.en: A whistleblower told the newspaper the factory was polluting the river.
ex.ko: 한 내부 고발자가 공장이 강을 오염시키고 있다고 신문사에 알렸다.

easy: A person who is not there or not at home.

ex.en: There were three absentees in class because of the flu.
ex.ko: 독감 때문에 반에 결석자가 세 명 있었다.

easy: Based on stories people tell, not on careful study.

ex.en: My grandma's anecdotal advice is that chicken soup cures colds.
ex.ko: 할머니의 경험담에 따르면 닭고기 수프가 감기를 낫게 한다.

easy: Not having enough red blood cells, which can make you tired and pale.

ex.en: The doctor said her anemia was why she felt so tired.
ex.ko: 의사는 그녀가 그렇게 피곤한 이유가 빈혈 때문이라고 했다.

easy: A strong feeling of not liking someone.

ex.en: There was animosity between the two teams after the close game.
ex.ko: 접전 끝에 두 팀 사이에 적대감이 생겼다.

easy: When the body's defense system attacks its own healthy parts by mistake.

ex.en: My aunt has an autoimmune illness that makes her joints hurt.
ex.ko: 이모는 관절이 아픈 자가 면역 질환을 앓고 있다.

easy: To throw lots of things at someone again and again.

ex.en: We bombarded each other with snowballs.
ex.ko: 우리는 서로에게 눈덩이를 마구 던졌다.

easy: To adjust a tool carefully so it measures correctly.

ex.en: The nurse calibrated the scale before weighing the babies.
ex.ko: 간호사는 아기들 몸무게를 재기 전에 저울 눈금을 맞추었다.

easy: A bottle for carrying water on hikes or trips.

ex.en: I filled my canteen at the stream.
ex.ko: 나는 시냇물에서 수통을 채웠다.

easy: A small electronic part that stores electricity for a short time.

ex.en: The robot kit came with resistors and a capacitor.
ex.ko: 로봇 키트에는 저항기와 축전기가 들어 있었다.

easy: In politics, in the middle, not far to the left or the right.

ex.en: The centrist leader tried to please both sides.
ex.ko: 중도파 지도자는 양쪽을 모두 만족시키려 했다.

easy: A person whose political ideas are in the middle.

ex.en: As a centrist, she listened to both parties before voting.
ex.ko: 중도파인 그녀는 투표하기 전에 양쪽 정당의 말을 모두 들었다.

easy: A person paid to drive someone else's car.

ex.en: The chauffeur opened the car door for the famous singer.
ex.ko: 운전기사가 유명 가수를 위해 차 문을 열어 주었다.

easy: To drive someone around in a car.

ex.en: Mom chauffeurs us to soccer, piano, and swimming every week.
ex.ko: 엄마는 매주 우리를 축구, 피아노, 수영에 태워 다니신다.

easy: A man who is a priest or minister in a Christian church.

ex.en: The clergyman blessed the animals at the pet festival.
ex.ko: 그 성직자는 반려동물 축제에서 동물들을 축복했다.

easy: A big round stadium with rows of seats going up all around.

ex.en: Thousands of fans filled the coliseum for the concert.
ex.ko: 수천 명의 팬이 콘서트를 보려고 원형 경기장을 가득 채웠다.

easy: To accept or forgive bad behavior instead of stopping it.

ex.en: Our school does not condone bullying.
ex.ko: 우리 학교는 괴롭힘을 용납하지 않는다.

easy: Too full, often with blood or fluid, so it feels stuffed.

ex.en: My nose was so congested that I could not smell my dinner.
ex.ko: 코가 꽉 막혀서 저녁 냄새를 맡을 수 없었다.

easy: A man who is a member of a city council.

ex.en: The councilman came to our school to talk about the new park.
ex.ko: 시의원이 새 공원에 대해 이야기하려고 우리 학교에 왔다.

easy: A small plant that grows sour red berries in wet places.

ex.en: Cranberries grow in boggy fields that farmers flood with water.
ex.ko: 크랜베리는 농부들이 물을 대는 습지 밭에서 자란다.

easy: A sweet, creamy food made of milk and eggs.

ex.en: Grandma made vanilla custard for dessert.
ex.ko: 할머니가 후식으로 바닐라 커스터드를 만드셨다.

easy: Careful talking about all sides of a question before deciding.

ex.en: After long deliberation, the class chose a name for the hamster.
ex.ko: 오랜 의논 끝에 반은 햄스터 이름을 정했다.

easy: Taking away government rules from a business.

ex.en: Deregulation let more airlines start flying.
ex.ko: 규제 완화로 더 많은 항공사가 운항을 시작했다.

easy: To leave someone who needs you.

ex.en: A good captain never deserts the crew.
ex.ko: 좋은 선장은 절대 선원들을 버리지 않는다.

easy: Empty and bare, with no shelter, food, or people.

ex.en: The desolate island had only rocks and a few birds.
ex.ko: 그 황량한 섬에는 바위와 새 몇 마리뿐이었다.

easy: A worker who digs.

ex.en: The diggers found an old coin while building the road.
ex.ko: 인부들이 길을 만들다가 오래된 동전을 발견했다.

easy: Getting rid of weapons or armies.

ex.en: The two countries agreed to disarmament to keep the peace.
ex.ko: 두 나라는 평화를 지키기 위해 군비 축소에 합의했다.

easy: Not being honest; lying or cheating.

ex.en: His dishonesty about the broken window got him in more trouble.
ex.ko: 깨진 창문에 대해 거짓말을 해서 그는 더 곤란해졌다.

easy: Moving apart in different directions from the same point.

ex.en: The divergence of the two paths made us choose left or right.
ex.ko: 두 길이 갈라져서 우리는 왼쪽과 오른쪽 중에 골라야 했다.

easy: To change a wild plant so it can be grown on farms.

ex.en: People domesticated wheat thousands of years ago.
ex.ko: 사람들은 수천 년 전에 밀을 작물화했다.

easy: Understood by only a small group of people with special knowledge.

ex.en: The book was full of esoteric words that only experts knew.
ex.ko: 그 책은 전문가만 아는 난해한 단어로 가득했다.

easy: Easy to catch fire.

ex.en: Keep flammable things like paper away from the stove.
ex.ko: 종이처럼 불에 잘 타는 것은 난로에서 멀리 두어라.

easy: To the greatest amount or most advanced point.

ex.en: Of all the kids, she went the furthest in the spelling bee.
ex.ko: 모든 아이들 중에서 그녀가 철자 맞히기 대회에서 가장 높이 올라갔다.

easy: Most far away.

ex.en: We sat in the furthest row from the stage.
ex.ko: 우리는 무대에서 가장 먼 줄에 앉았다.

easy: A dark red stone used in jewelry.

ex.en: January's birthstone is a deep red garnet.
ex.ko: 1월의 탄생석은 짙은 빨간색 석류석이다.

easy: A tree that grows big, round, sour-sweet yellow fruit.

ex.en: The grapefruit tree in Grandma's yard is full of fruit.
ex.ko: 할머니 마당의 자몽나무에 열매가 가득 열렸다.

easy: A tall, thin, very fast dog often used in races.

ex.en: The greyhound zoomed around the track after the toy rabbit.
ex.ko: 그레이하운드가 장난감 토끼를 쫓아 트랙을 쌩 돌았다.

easy: A place where there is trouble and fighting might break out.

ex.en: Reporters were sent to the world's hotspots.
ex.ko: 기자들이 세계 곳곳의 분쟁 지역으로 파견되었다.

easy: Impossible to explain or understand.
ko: 이해할 수 없는, 설명할 수 없는

ex.en: For some incomprehensible reason, my sock was in the fridge.
ex.ko: 무슨 영문인지 모르게 내 양말이 냉장고에 들어 있었다.

easy: When a place is filled with pests like bugs or mice.

ex.en: We had an ant infestation in the kitchen this summer.
ex.ko: 올여름 우리 부엌에 개미가 들끓었다.

easy: A very strong man who can keep going for a very long time.

ex.en: Grandpa is an ironman who still runs every morning at 80.
ex.ko: 할아버지는 여든인데도 아침마다 달리시는 철인이다.

easy: From or about Jordan, a country in the Middle East.

ex.en: We saw the old Jordanian city of Petra, carved into pink rock.
ex.ko: 우리는 분홍빛 바위를 깎아 만든 요르단의 고대 도시 페트라를 보았다.

easy: A person from Jordan, a country in the Middle East.

ex.en: The Jordanian guide led us through the desert.
ex.ko: 요르단 사람 안내원이 우리를 사막으로 안내했다.

easy: A worm that lives in water and sticks to animals to suck their blood.

ex.en: After swimming in the pond, I found a leech on my leg.
ex.ko: 연못에서 수영하고 나서 다리에 거머리가 붙어 있는 걸 발견했다.

easy: A hard, dry Italian cheese often grated over pasta.

ex.en: I sprinkled Parmesan on my spaghetti.
ex.ko: 나는 스파게티에 파르메산 치즈를 뿌렸다.

easy: A person who happens to walk by.

ex.en: A passer stopped to help when my bike chain fell off.
ex.ko: 자전거 체인이 빠지자 지나가던 사람이 멈춰서 도와주었다.

easy: A big seabird with a huge beak that has a pouch for catching fish.

ex.en: The pelican scooped up a fish in its giant beak.
ex.ko: 펠리컨이 커다란 부리로 물고기를 떠 올렸다.

easy: A person who gets regular money after they stop working, usually because they are old.

ex.en: The pensioner spends his mornings feeding ducks at the park.
ex.ko: 그 연금 수령자는 아침마다 공원에서 오리에게 먹이를 준다.

easy: An area of a country run by its own leader, like in Japan or France.

ex.en: Kyoto is a prefecture in Japan.
ex.ko: 교토는 일본의 한 현이다.

easy: Trying to look more important or fancy than it really is.

ex.en: The pretentious house had gold statues on the front lawn.
ex.ko: 그 허세 가득한 집 앞마당에는 금빛 조각상들이 있었다.

easy: A friendly feeling of understanding and trust between people.

ex.en: Our teacher has a great rapport with every student.
ex.ko: 우리 선생님은 모든 학생과 아주 친밀한 관계를 맺고 계신다.

easy: Great damage or destruction.

ex.en: The old castle showed the ravages of time and weather.
ex.ko: 오래된 성에는 세월과 비바람에 망가진 흔적이 남아 있었다.

easy: A person who writes the story and words for movies.

ex.en: The screenwriter wrote a funny movie about a talking dog.
ex.ko: 그 시나리오 작가는 말하는 개에 관한 재미있는 영화를 썼다.

easy: A big fishing net that hangs straight down in the water, with floats on top and weights on the bottom.

ex.en: The fishermen pulled the seine to shore, full of fish.
ex.ko: 어부들이 물고기로 가득한 후릿그물을 해변으로 끌어당겼다.

easy: A person who chooses or picks.

ex.en: The team selector picked me to play goalie.
ex.ko: 선수를 고르는 사람이 나를 골키퍼로 뽑았다.

easy: A large piece of cloth worn over the shoulders or head to keep warm.

ex.en: Grandma wrapped her shawl around her shoulders on the cold porch.
ex.ko: 할머니는 추운 현관에서 숄을 어깨에 두르셨다.

easy: The main kind of money used in Uganda.

ex.en: The bananas at the market cost a few hundred shillings.
ex.ko: 시장의 바나나는 몇백 실링이었다.

easy: To cover or hide something completely.

ex.en: The mountain was shrouded in thick fog.
ex.ko: 산이 짙은 안개에 뒤덮여 있었다.

easy: A person from Slovakia, a country in central Europe.

ex.en: Our new Slovak classmate taught us how to say "hello."
ex.ko: 새로 온 슬로바키아 친구가 우리에게 "안녕"이라고 말하는 법을 가르쳐 주었다.

easy: On the right side of a ship or plane, when facing the front.

ex.en: We waved from the starboard deck as the ship left.
ex.ko: 배가 떠날 때 우리는 오른쪽 갑판에서 손을 흔들었다.

easy: The right side of a ship or plane when you face the front.

ex.en: "Whale to starboard!" shouted the captain.
ex.ko: "우현에 고래다!" 선장이 외쳤다.

easy: Showing a common, fixed idea about a type of person or thing, without anything fresh or original.

ex.en: The movie had a stereotypical nerd with big glasses.
ex.ko: 그 영화에는 큰 안경을 쓴 판에 박힌 모범생 캐릭터가 나왔다.

easy: A person from a group of people in southeastern India who speak Telugu.

ex.en: My Telugu friend taught me to count to ten in her language.
ex.ko: 텔루구족 친구가 자기네 말로 열까지 세는 법을 가르쳐 주었다.

easy: To hurt someone's feelings so badly that they stay upset or scared for a long time.

ex.en: The loud storm traumatized the puppy, and it hid for days.
ex.ko: 요란한 폭풍에 겁에 질린 강아지는 며칠 동안 숨어 있었다.

easy: Not yet explored or mapped.

ex.en: The explorers sailed into uncharted waters.
ex.ko: 탐험가들은 지도에 없는 바다로 항해해 나아갔다.

easy: Not expected; nobody saw it coming.

ex.en: An unforeseen snowstorm closed the school.
ex.ko: 예상치 못한 눈보라로 학교가 문을 닫았다.

easy: Not signed with a name.

ex.en: The unsigned note just said "Happy birthday!"
ex.ko: 서명 없는 쪽지에는 "생일 축하해!"라고만 쓰여 있었다.

easy: Understood without being said out loud.

ex.en: We had an unspoken rule never to tell Mom about the surprise.
ex.ko: 우리에게는 엄마에게 깜짝 선물 이야기를 절대 하지 않는다는 무언의 규칙이 있었다.

easy: A man servant who helps his employer with clothes and daily needs.

ex.en: The valet laid out the prince's clothes each morning.
ex.ko: 시종은 매일 아침 왕자의 옷을 준비해 두었다.

easy: In a very strong, forceful way.

ex.en: He vehemently said he did not eat the last cookie.
ex.ko: 그는 마지막 쿠키를 자기가 먹지 않았다고 강하게 말했다.

easy: Weak and lacking strength in the body.

ex.en: The weakly kitten was too small to climb the steps.
ex.ko: 허약한 아기 고양이는 너무 작아서 계단을 오를 수 없었다.

easy: In a weak way, without much strength.

ex.en: The tired puppy wagged its tail weakly.
ex.ko: 지친 강아지가 힘없이 꼬리를 흔들었다.

easy: A long, smooth sausage, often eaten in a bun.

ex.en: We roasted wieners over the campfire.
ex.ko: 우리는 모닥불에 소시지를 구웠다.

easy: A member of a city council.

ex.en: The alderman cut the ribbon to open the new library.
ex.ko: 시의원이 리본을 잘라 새 도서관을 개관했다.

easy: Feeling left out and separate from other people.

ex.en: The new student felt alienation until he made friends.
ex.ko: 새로 온 학생은 친구를 사귈 때까지 소외감을 느꼈다.

easy: An illness where a person eats far too little and gets dangerously thin.

ex.en: Doctors and family helped her recover from anorexia.
ex.ko: 의사와 가족이 그녀가 거식증을 이겨 내도록 도왔다.

easy: A scientist who studies people and how they live in different cultures.

ex.en: The anthropologist lived with a village family to learn their customs.
ex.ko: 인류학자는 마을 사람들의 풍습을 배우려고 한 가족과 함께 살았다.

easy: A medicine that helps people with depression feel better.

ex.en: The doctor gave her an antidepressant to help her mood.
ex.ko: 의사는 그녀의 기분이 나아지도록 항우울제를 처방했다.

easy: Wearing away by rubbing.

ex.en: Attrition from the river smoothed the sharp rocks.
ex.ko: 강물에 깎여 날카로운 바위가 매끄러워졌다.

easy: Doing things without really thinking about them.

ex.en: I was so sleepy that I brushed my teeth on autopilot.
ex.ko: 너무 졸려서 아무 생각 없이 이를 닦았다.

easy: Loose and hanging, not tight.

ex.en: He wore baggy pants that dragged on the ground.
ex.ko: 그는 땅에 끌리는 헐렁한 바지를 입었다.

easy: Heavy stuff put in the bottom of a ship to keep it steady.

ex.en: The ship carried rocks as ballast so it wouldn't tip over.
ex.ko: 배는 뒤집히지 않도록 바닥짐으로 돌을 실었다.

easy: To make a ship steady by adding heavy stuff to the bottom.

ex.en: The sailors ballasted the boat with sandbags.
ex.ko: 선원들은 모래주머니로 배에 바닥짐을 실었다.

easy: The blood flowing through your body.

ex.en: Medicine from a shot goes into your bloodstream.
ex.ko: 주사로 맞은 약은 혈류로 들어간다.

easy: A kind of grass often used for lawns and to feed animals.

ex.en: Horses graze on the bluegrass in Kentucky.
ex.ko: 켄터키에서는 말들이 블루그래스를 뜯어 먹는다.

easy: About a budget, a plan for spending money.

ex.en: The class trip was canceled for budgetary reasons.
ex.ko: 학급 여행은 예산 문제로 취소되었다.

easy: Cloth with green, brown, and black spots that help you blend in with nature.

ex.en: My brother wore a camo jacket to go bird-watching.
ex.ko: 형은 새를 관찰하러 갈 때 위장무늬 재킷을 입었다.

easy: To cheer and lead the crowd at a sports game.

ex.en: My sister cheerleads at every football game.
ex.ko: 언니는 모든 미식축구 경기에서 치어리더로 응원한다.

easy: A saying used so often that it is boring and no longer means much.

ex.en: "Every cloud has a silver lining" is a cliché.
ex.ko: "모든 구름에는 은빛 테두리가 있다"는 진부한 말이다.

easy: A brown, flat bug that comes out at night and can live in houses.

ex.en: Mom screamed when a cockroach ran across the kitchen floor.
ex.ko: 바퀴벌레가 부엌 바닥을 가로지르자 엄마가 비명을 질렀다.

easy: Hard to carry or use because it is big or heavy.

ex.en: The cumbersome box was too big to fit through the door.
ex.ko: 그 거추장스러운 상자는 너무 커서 문으로 들어가지 않았다.

easy: Rudely short when talking.

ex.en: The busy clerk gave a curt answer and turned away.
ex.ko: 바쁜 점원은 퉁명스럽게 대답하고 돌아섰다.

easy: Happening again and again in a repeating pattern.

ex.en: The seasons are cyclical: spring, summer, fall, winter, and back again.
ex.ko: 계절은 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울을 거쳐 다시 돌아오는 순환을 한다.

easy: A change in shape that makes something worse or twisted.

ex.en: The heat caused deformation of the plastic cup.
ex.ko: 열 때문에 플라스틱 컵이 일그러졌다.

easy: Used for praying or worship.

ex.en: Grandma reads a devotional book every morning.
ex.ko: 할머니는 매일 아침 기도서를 읽으신다.

easy: A short religious service or time of prayer.

ex.en: Our camp started each day with a short devotional.
ex.ko: 우리 캠프는 매일 짧은 예배로 하루를 시작했다.
